clue.text: Composer curtailed excessive desire to straddle horse

indicators.note: to straddle is to sit with legs either side, so the shortened word goes around the other piece
something curtailed has its tail cut off, so the final letter of the word for excessive desire goes

parts.note: a mania is an excessive desire or craze
horse and scag are both slang names for heroin

explanation.surface: A composer whose excessive appetite for riding has been cut short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is not an animal here but drug slang for heroin; 'curtailed' and 'to straddle' work on the craze word and the drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Pietro Mascagni was the Italian who wrote the opera Cavalleria rusticana.

clue.text: Northern town backed concert with character from the past

indicators.note: backed means sent backwards, so the word for concert is read in reverse

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert, like the BBC Proms
eth is an Old English letter no longer in use

explanation.surface: A northern town supported a concert featuring a historical figure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' looks like 'supported' but turns PROM into MORP. 'character' is a letter of an alphabet, not a person. Morpeth is a market town in Northumberland.
explanation.definitionFit: Morpeth is a market town in Northumberland in the north of England.

clue.text: Go home exhausted, chiefly, after regular visit to star's grave

indicators.note: after places the alternate letters of star before what follows
regular takes letters at regular intervals, here alternate ones from star

parts.note: to turn in is to go home to bed

indicators.note: chiefly takes the head, the first letter, of exhausted

explanation.surface: A tired fan heads home after a regular visit to a celebrity's burial place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective, solemn. 'regular' takes S and A from 'star', and 'chiefly' gives E.
explanation.definitionFit: Saturnine means gloomy and serious in temperament, once linked to the influence of the planet Saturn.

clue.text: Innocent woman's found clutching headless corpse

indicators.note: clutching means holding, so the name goes around the other piece

parts.note: Anne is a woman's name

indicators.note: headless removes the first letter of the word for corpse

parts.note: a body is a corpse

explanation.surface: A woman discovered holding a decapitated body, though she is supposedly guiltless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Innocent' means harmless here, not guiltless; 'headless' and 'found clutching' cut and wrap the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Anodyne means harmless and inoffensive, unlikely to provoke anyone.

clue.text: Greg of course is associated with introduction of Space Invaders

parts.note: Greg Norman is an Australian golfer, and a golf course is his territory

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its first letter, from Space

explanation.surface: A golfer linked to the launch of the arcade game Space Invaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of course' means on the golf course, not 'naturally'. 'introduction of' gives S. 'Space Invaders' tempts as one name, but the definition is 'Invaders' alone: the Normans conquered England in 1066.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans were the invading army that conquered England under William in 1066.

clue.text: Make use of extremely desperate tactic

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken from desperate

parts.note: a ploy is a cunning tactic or manoeuvre

explanation.surface: Someone resorting to a last-ditch manoeuvre out of sheer desperation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' looks like it intensifies 'desperate', but it picks that word's first and last letters, D and E.
explanation.definitionFit: To deploy something is to bring it into action or put it to use.

clue.text: Unearths most of public housing records? On the contrary

indicators.note: housing means containing, so the records word holds the other piece

parts.note: discs are gramophone records

indicators.note: most of a word drops its last letter

parts.note: overt means open or public

explanation.surface: A suggestion that public housing mostly finds its way into the records, or the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the clue's order, so the records hold the public, not the other way round; 'most of' and 'housing' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To discover something is to find it out or bring it to light.

clue.text: Arvo? It's used by Australian in noted composition

parts.note: Arvo Part is an Estonian composer, so his first name points to his surname
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arvo is the Australian slang word for afternoon, used in a piece of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arvo' is Australian slang for afternoon, which the clue plays on, but it is the first name of the composer Arvo Part. 'noted' means set to musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: A partita is a piece of instrumental music, such as a suite for solo violin by Bach.

clue.text: National radio broadcast introduces Mahler's Fourth and Ninth, maybe

indicators.note: introduces means comes before, so the jumbled letters precede the final piece
broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order
Fourth picks out the fourth letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: A national radio station airs two Mahler symphonies.
explanation.walkthrough: The Mahler symphonies are a red herring: 'Fourth' takes the fourth letter of Mahler, L. 'broadcast' rearranges N and RADIO to ORDINA.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninth is an example of an ordinal number, one that gives position in a sequence.

clue.text: Go back, with rot setting in?

definitions.text: Go back, with rot setting in?

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged letters are put inside the word for go back

parts.note: to regress is to go back to an earlier state

indicators.note: setting, as of jelly or concrete, changes the shape of the word rot, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about something deteriorating as decay takes hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setting' (as jelly sets into a new shape) and 'in' do the work. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: going backwards as things decay.
explanation.definitionFit: To retrogress is to move backwards or decline into a worse condition, which is what happens when rot sets in.

clue.text: You need some proper identification to travel

indicators.note: some of the words is a part of them, so the answer is a run of letters across proper identification

explanation.surface: Being told you must show valid ID before you can board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' points to a run of letters inside 'proper identification': propeR IDEntification.
explanation.definitionFit: To ride is to travel on a horse, bike or vehicle.

clue.text: Evacuation at dawn? It's seldom discussed in Parliament

definitions.meaning: humorously, a bowel movement first thing in the morning
a backbench Commons motion that is tabled but almost never debated

explanation.walkthrough: 'Evacuation' suggests people fleeing, but here it means emptying the bowels; motion is a polite word for a bowel movement. An early day motion is a UK House of Commons motion that MPs sign but rarely debate.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally, the phrase is a bowel movement at an early hour; formally it is a British parliamentary notice that is seldom given debating time.

clue.text: One beset by present setbacks loses heart, but she'll succeed

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the word for present goes around the letter for one

parts.note: present means here, as in answering a register
one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: a word that loses its heart keeps only its outside letters, here from setbacks

explanation.surface: Someone facing current reverses who becomes dispirited, yet is determined to win through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beset by' puts I inside HERE, and 'loses heart' strips setbacks to its first and last letters, S and S. 'succeed' means inherit, not triumph.
explanation.definitionFit: An heiress is a woman who inherits, so she will succeed to the property or title.

clue.text: Increase in turnover's recent? Above all it's supply and demand

indicators.note: above all puts the jumbled letters at the top of this down entry
supply here is the adverb, in a supple way, so the letters bend into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, without the apostrophe

indicators.note: in turnover means turned over, so the word for increase is read backwards

parts.note: to up something is to increase it
late means recent, as in the late news

explanation.surface: An economist claims a rise in turnover is recent and blames market forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' looks like the economic noun, but is the adverb from supple, rearranging ITS to STI. 'in turnover's' turns UP to PU.
explanation.definitionFit: To stipulate is to demand or specify something as a condition of an agreement.

clue.text: Vehicle reversed by inexperienced driver into river? A disaster!

indicators.note: into tells us the other pieces go inside the river's name

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Scotland and in Wales

indicators.note: reversed means the word for the vehicle is read from back to front

parts.note: a cab is a taxi, a vehicle
L is the learner plate on a British novice driver's car

explanation.surface: A learner backs a car into a river: a calamity.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver shows an L plate; 'reversed' and 'into' place the pieces in the Scottish river.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden, humiliating failure or fiasco.

clue.text: Copper wire found lying around on street

indicators.note: lying around means wrapped round, so the wire word encloses the other pieces

parts.note: a cable is a wire

explanation.surface: Copper wire discovered abandoned in the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like the metal, but it is slang for a police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Copper is British slang for a police officer, and a constable is the lowest police rank.

clue.text: Cicely's relation is nouveau riche, very loud at first

indicators.note: nouveau means new, so the letters are given a new arrangement
at first takes the opening letter of each of very and loud

explanation.surface: Someone called Cicely has a vulgar, newly wealthy relative who shouts.
explanation.walkthrough: Cicely is not a person but sweet cicely, a herb in the same family. 'nouveau' rearranges RICHE together with V and L, the first letters picked out by 'at first'.
explanation.definitionFit: Chervil and sweet cicely are related aromatic herbs of the carrot family.

clue.text: Disruptive sort left after mild expression of annoyance by leading lady

indicators.note: after places the letter for left following the exclamation

parts.note: heck is a mild substitute for a swearword
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the queen, the leading lady of the land

explanation.surface: An unruly person storms out after the star actress mutters in irritation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leading lady' suggests an actress, but in crosswords ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A heckler disrupts a speaker or performer with interruptions and jeers.

clue.text: Screen saver ultimately needs former operating system before being installed

indicators.note: being installed means put in place inside, so the word for before goes within the other letters
ultimately takes the final letter of the word saver

parts.note: DOS was the disk operating system used on early PCs
ere is an old word for before

explanation.surface: Computer jargon about a screen saver needing an old operating system set up first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen saver' looks like one computer term, but 'Screen' is the definition and 'saver' only gives its last letter, R; 'being installed' places the old word for before.
explanation.definitionFit: A reredos is an ornamental screen behind a church altar.

clue.text: French art scene's eccentric character

parts.note: art is the old form of are, as in thou art, and the French for thou art is tu es

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, so the letters of scene are jumbled

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A remark about the quirky character of the French art world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'art' is the verb (thou art), not painting. 'eccentric' rearranges SCENE to SENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Essence is the fundamental nature or character of something.

clue.text: Ravel Bolero at heart a bore? It depends on the listener

indicators.note: ravel means to tangle, so the letters are knotted into a new order
at heart takes the central letters of Bolero

explanation.surface: A listener judging whether the core of Ravel's Bolero is tedious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ravel' is not the composer but the verb, to tangle. 'at heart' gives LE from Bolero; the definition plays on 'depends' as hangs down from the ear.
explanation.definitionFit: The soft lobe hangs from the bottom of the ear, the organ of anyone who listens.

clue.text: Chap's rung by ambassador to Norway

parts.note: a rung of a ladder is a step
HE is His Excellency, the title of an ambassador
N is the international vehicle code for Norway

explanation.surface: A man is telephoned by the Norwegian ambassador.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rung' looks like the past of ring, a phone call, but it is a ladder step.
explanation.definitionFit: Stephen is a man's name, and a chap is a man.

clue.text: One disappearing from air, involved in going around Earth

definitions.text: One disappearing from air, involved in going around Earth

indicators.note: involved in means wrapped inside, so the shortened word goes within the rearranged letters
going around means turned about, so the letters of earth are rearranged
disappearing from means the letter for one is taken out of air

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: An aviator vanished from the sky while attempting to fly around the world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disappearing from', 'involved in' and 'going around' work the pieces, and the whole clue describes Amelia Earhart, lost in 1937 trying to circle the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Amelia Earhart, the American aviator, vanished over the Pacific in 1937 during a round-the-world flight.

clue.text: Several people will be sent this description of second-in-command

definitions.text: Several people will be sent this
definitions.meaning: a single message copied to many recipients
the second letter in the word command is O, a round letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'second-in-command' looks like a deputy, but it is the second letter of 'command', O, which is circular.
explanation.definitionFit: A circular letter is a mailing sent to many people at once; and O is round in shape.

clue.text: Make slow progress in Latin in school

indicators.note: the second in places the letter for Latin inside the word for school

parts.note: a school of whales or dolphins is also called a pod

explanation.surface: Slow going for a pupil struggling with Latin lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'school' is a group of sea creatures, not a place of education.
explanation.definitionFit: To plod is to walk or work slowly and laboriously.

clue.text: Rising alarm?

parts.note: fear felt as you climb higher, not an alarm clock waking you

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising alarm' suggests an alarm clock; it is dread that grows with altitude. AEROPHOBIA was a tempting alternative but means fear of flying.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrophobia is the fear of heights, a terror that increases the higher one goes.

clue.text: Short time out of water-a couple of seconds — hurt fish

indicators.note: hurt means damaged, so the remaining letters are knocked into a new order
out of means the letter for time is taken out of the word water

parts.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
S is the abbreviation for second, so two of them give SS

explanation.surface: A fish briefly stranded out of water for a couple of seconds and injured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of' removes T from WATER, leaving WAER; add SS, and 'hurt' rearranges the lot.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish found around rocky coasts.

clue.text: Head of retail outlet imports a German design again

indicators.note: imports means brings inside, so the German word goes within the other letters
the head of a word is its first letter, here from retail

parts.note: a vent is an outlet for air or gas
ein is German for a

explanation.surface: The boss of a shop brings in a German product design once more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imports' sounds like trade, but it is the container signal: the German article goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvent something is to create or devise it afresh.
